title: Semantic search: finding by meaning, not by exact word

videos.script: Lesson one ended with a customer's question and an article that answered it in other words. This lesson builds the search that finds it. {{question}} First, the search it has to beat. A proper keyword search ranks articles by the words they share with the question. It finds an order number at once. It cannot find an answer written in other words. {{keyword}} Then the search by meaning. Every article is embedded once, ahead of time, and stored. {{index}} Each question is embedded when it arrives and compared with every stored vector. The closest come back first. {{query}} Then you will measure both, on twenty-four questions with known answers. You will count how often the right article comes first, and how often it makes the top three. {{measure}} Long pages need cutting into pieces, or one vector blurs three subjects into none. {{chunks}} And finally you will merge the two searches into one ranking. The merge rescues the exact strings, and it costs something too. You will see exactly what. {{hybrid}} By the end, you will have a working search, and a number that says how good it is. {{end}}
